key_insight: Specialized, physics-driven machine learning force fields are needed to make MLIPs reliable for complex materials dynamics beyond near-equilibrium prediction.
engineering_relevance: For fracture and damage modeling, task-specific ML force fields can extend atomistic simulation to larger scales and more realistic loading, but they must be validated against the exact observables of interest.
method: Assess MLIP trade-offs for strained, reactive, and open-system configurations.
Use specialized adaptations for nonlocal, field-coupled, and multiphase dynamics.
Benchmark universal foundation models and task-specific potentials on application-specific targets.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes four demanding validation contexts—electrified interfaces, open systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture—to argue that observable-specific benchmarking is essential.
watch_item: High-order architectures and missing nonlocal physics can add major computational cost and bias results if the model is not matched to the intended dynamical regime.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
